entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-2h46-9x5w-4wf7: Entire CLI: Path traversal in checkpoint session metadata allows arbitrary file write during resume/rewind
entry.content:
Entire CLI: Path traversal in checkpoint session metadata allows arbitrary file write during resume/rewind

Aliases: CVE-2026-57208, GO-2026-5063

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:A/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:H/SA:H

Affected:

  • github.com/entireio/cli — fixed in 0.7.7

### Impact A path traversal vulnerability in Entire CLI allows an attacker with push access to the checkpoints repository to craft malicious checkpoint metadata that causes `entire session resume` or `entire checkpoint rewind` to write attacker-controlled transcript data outside of the expected session directory. The issue occurs because checkpoint metadata is fetched from the remote `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch and the `SessionID` field was used to construct filesystem paths without validation in the restore path. A malicious `SessionID` containing absolute paths or path traversal sequences could cause arbitrary files on the victim’s machine to be overwritten. ### Patches The patched versions (`v0.7.7` or `v0.7.8-nightly.*`) observe stronger input validation and enforce traversal-re…

chi: Client IP spoofing in ClientIPFromXFF via X-Forwarded-For

Aliases: CVE-2026-114437

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/go-chi/chi/v5 — fixed in 5.4.0

### Summary `ClientIPFromXFF` skips any `X-Forwarded-For` entry in a configured trusted CIDR but never verifies that the direct TCP peer in `http.Request.RemoteAddr` belongs to that CIDR. The attack is remote and requires one unauthenticated HTTP request with no user interaction (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N). It changes security decisions and exposes one protected handler within the same application (S:U/C:L/I:L); no availability loss was observed (A:N). **Preconditions:** The application uses `ClientIPFromXFF` and makes the origin server reachable by an anonymous client outside the configured trusted-proxy CIDRs. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-cxf3-9h37-7rr8: Echo: Rejected WebSocket upgrades can bypass Echo route-level access controls
entry.content:
Echo: Rejected WebSocket upgrades can bypass Echo route-level access controls

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • github.com/labstack/echo/v4 — fixed in 4.16.1
  • github.com/labstack/echo/v5 — fixed in 5.4.1

## Impact Echo's Proxy middleware selected a raw tunnel when the client requested a WebSocket upgrade, before validating whether the configured upstream accepted it. If the upstream returned an ordinary HTTP response and kept the connection alive, subsequent HTTP requests on that connection were forwarded directly to the same upstream without passing through Echo's router or route-specific middleware. This can bypass authentication or authorization enforced only at Echo's routes. Exploitation requires an accessible proxy route, an upstream that rejects the upgrade without closing the connection, and a target resource on that upstream without independent authorization. The issue does not provide arbitrary-host proxying or bypass the upstream's own authentication. ## Affected versions and…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-f48p-c9v4-h7xv: Echo: BodyDump captures request and response bodies without size limits in v4
entry.content:
Echo: BodyDump captures request and response bodies without size limits in v4

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • github.com/labstack/echo/v4 — fixed in 4.16.1

## Impact Echo v4's opt-in BodyDump middleware read complete request bodies into memory and retained complete response bodies without a capture limit. A client able to submit large requests to a route using BodyDump could cause large allocations before the application handler ran. Large responses, including responses whose size can be influenced by a client, also caused an additional unbounded capture allocation. Repeated or concurrent requests can exhaust process memory and cause denial of service. BodyDump is not enabled by default. Deployments with effective request limits may reduce the request-side exposure; response capture requires separate consideration. ## Affected versions and patch Echo v4 versions through v4.16.0 are affected. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-x9ff-22gv-65f4: Echo: BodyDump can discard BodyLimit overflow errors for unknown-length requests
entry.content:
Echo: BodyDump can discard BodyLimit overflow errors for unknown-length requests

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • github.com/labstack/echo/v5 — fixed in 5.4.1

## Impact Echo v5's BodyDump middleware captured a bounded prefix, drained the remaining request body while ignoring read errors, and then replaced the body with the captured prefix. With an outer BodyLimit, an unknown-length request such as an HTTP/1.1 chunked request, and a BodyDump capture limit below the BodyLimit threshold, an overflow detected during that drain could be discarded. The handler could consequently process a truncated request and return success even though the original body exceeded the configured limit. This is a conditional size-policy bypass; no general authentication bypass, production data modification or denial of service is claimed. Known-length requests rejected before BodyDump runs are unaffected by this path. ## Affected versions and patch All v5 releases f…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-9969-6676-49h5: Echo: WebSocket proxy can retain connections and handlers after client disconnect
entry.content:
Echo: WebSocket proxy can retain connections and handlers after client disconnect

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • github.com/labstack/echo/v4 — fixed in 4.16.1
  • github.com/labstack/echo/v5 — fixed in 5.4.1

## Impact Echo's Proxy middleware could retain a handler, copy goroutines and network connections after a WebSocket client disconnected if the upstream kept its connection open. The raw proxy waited for both copy directions to finish without reliably closing the other connection when one direction ended. Rejected upgrade responses with HTTP keep-alive were one way to trigger this behavior. Repeated connections can accumulate resources and cause denial of service. The impact depends on the proxy route's accessibility, upstream behavior and configured connection deadlines. This is a medium-severity resource-retention issue; no confidentiality or integrity impact is claimed. ## Affected versions and patch Affected versions are v4.15.0 through v4.16.0 and v5.0.0 through v5.4.0. The regress…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-h7wr-284f-5qvc: Echo: Decompress permits unbounded gzip expansion in v4
entry.content:
Echo: Decompress permits unbounded gzip expansion in v4

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • github.com/labstack/echo/v4 — fixed in 4.16.1

## Impact Echo v4's opt-in Decompress middleware exposed a gzip-decoded request stream without limiting its expanded size. A small compressed request could therefore produce a very large decoded body. Handlers that read or bind that body could consume excessive memory or CPU, and repeated or concurrent requests could cause denial of service. The middleware is not enabled by default. A limit on the compressed request size alone does not bound the decompressed size. Applications that already apply an effective body limit after decompression have reduced exposure. ## Affected versions and patch Echo v4 versions through v4.16.0 are affected. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-h53f-rm2w-w7rg: Echo: X-Real-IP extractor trusts the header value instead of the sending peer
entry.content:
Echo: X-Real-IP extractor trusts the header value instead of the sending peer

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/labstack/echo/v5 — fixed in 5.4.1

## Impact In Echo v5, `ExtractIPFromRealIPHeader` checked whether the address supplied in `X-Real-IP` belonged to a trusted range instead of checking the address of the direct network peer. An untrusted client could therefore supply a loopback or private address and have it returned by `c.RealIP()` with the extractor's default trust options. Applications using this extractor for IP allowlists, IP-based rate limiting, audit logs or forwarding headers could accept a spoofed client identity. Exploitation requires that the attacker can reach Echo directly or that an intervening proxy passes through the attacker's `X-Real-IP` value. Applications using the default direct IP extractor are unaffected. Echo v4 is unaffected by this v5 regression. ## Affected versions and patch All v5 releases f…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-c8w8-3pqp-wr83: SiYuan: A parser differential between the WebSocket keepalive exemption and the session quarantine allows unauthenticated access to the broadcast event stream

SiYuan: A parser differential between the WebSocket keepalive exemption and the session quarantine allows unauthenticated access to the broadcast event stream

Aliases: CVE-2026-73054

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/siyuan-note/siyuan/kernel — fixed in 0.0.0-20260731131820-67bc300b6ea6

### Summary Two checks on the same WebSocket request URI parse it differently. The authentication exemption for keepalive sessions matches raw substrings, while the quarantine introduced to contain those sessions reads a parsed query parameter. Because Go's `url.Values.Get` returns only the first value for a repeated key, a single URI can satisfy the exemption and still resolve to a non-auth session identity. ## Summary `installBazaarPlugin` (and the equivalent endpoints for widgets/icons/templates/themes) accept `packageName`, `repoURL`, and `repoHash` as independent request fields with no validation that they refer to the same package. `packageName` alone determines the install destination; `repoURL`/`repoHash` alone determine what content gets downloaded and written there. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-4pjg-x8qj-33j5: SiYuan: authFilePublishAccess distinguishes hidden and forbidden documents from public and nonexistent ones, and issues a publish-auth cookie for documents it reports as forbidden
entry.content:
SiYuan: authFilePublishAccess distinguishes hidden and forbidden documents from public and nonexistent ones, and issues a publish-auth cookie for documents it reports as forbidden

Aliases: CVE-2026-73630

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/siyuan-note/siyuan/kernel — fixed in 0.0.0-20260731093152-c7522b8db586

### Summary `/api/filetree/authFilePublishAccess` is registered with `CheckAuth` only and is reachable anonymously. It never sets a failure code, so its outcome is signalled entirely by the response message and by whether a `Set-Cookie` header is present. Those two signals differ across access tiers, which lets an anonymous caller determine, for any candidate document identifier, whether that document is public or nonexistent, password-protected, or exists at the hidden or forbidden tier. Separately, hidden and forbidden entries carry an empty password. Submitting `password:""` therefore satisfies the equality check for them, and the server responds by issuing `Set-Cookie: publish-auth-<docID>` for a document whose own tier is forbidden. ### Details **Route,** identical on both refs: …
